The chart app has two direct callers of `useAbortController`, both in exported workspace forms. A third chart file reaches it indirectly through `useOpenmrsSWR`.

**Direct users in openmrs-esm-patient-chart**

1. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx`: `ExportedVitalsAndBiometricsForm` (lines 64–699) calls `useAbortController()` at line 87. Its abort controller is not passed to any request in the parts I read, so the effect is limited to the component's lifecycle.
2. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/lab-results/exported-lab-results-form.workspace.tsx`: `ExportedLabResultsForm` (lines 63–464) calls `useAbortController()` at line 70. The import is at line 12.

**Indirect users in the chart app**

3. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-banner-app/src/hooks/usePersonAttributes.ts` calls `useOpenmrsSWR` at line 16. `useOpenmrsSWR` calls `useAbortController` internally (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useOpenmrsSWR.ts:72`), so a behaviour change there would reach this hook. I did not read the hook's full body, so the line range is only the call site.

**Other consumers of the hook in openmrs-esm-core** (not chart code, but they would be affected by the same change)

- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useAbortController.ts:25`, the hook itself. It creates a new controller when the current one is aborted and aborts it on unmount.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useOpenmrsSWR.ts:72`, which uses it internally.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-primary-navigation-app/src/components/change-language/change-language.modal.tsx:33`, which calls it directly.

My checkout contains only the chart repo, so the core and chart paths above come from Falkon search. The chart and core searches each returned all matches for their repo. I did not check the other 40 repos for indirect use of `useOpenmrsSWR` and would need more search calls to do that.
